This is the merge of PR #6, a bundle of "pre-pilot" fixes for the MedRecord app, and it is associated with the P3 (patient visit-record detail) work stream, so no separate story lookup was needed. Four things are claimed and the diff backs up each: (1) the patient-facing screens P2–P5 were switched from hard-coded placeholder ("mock") data to real backend calls, with loading and error handling added and the developer-only demo toggle buttons removed; (2) four cross-screen "integration" bugs are fixed — newly created patients can now log in, doctor-created visits appear in the patient's timeline, the patient can see and revoke a doctor's access, and a crash path in the Expo Go test environment is guarded; (3) the one-time passcode (OTP) resend cooldown was shortened from 45 to 30 seconds on both login screens per a locked product decision; and (4) the backend now rejects any attempt to change a patient's mobile number, since that number is the patient's unique key. The merge also carries documentation: a new "Integration Tester" agent definition, the integration-test session log, PM and security review notes, and a lessons write-up about gaps a human owner caught after the project was declared complete. The included review documents state that P3/P5 were device-verified (4 of 4 checks), integration testing passed 6 of 7 scenarios with 1 deliberately skipped, and a security re-check cleared the mobile-number guard; I am relaying what those documents say, not anything I executed or confirmed myself. The code reads as complete and consistent with the commit's description, so this is "Code complete" rather than "Tested": the team's own notes flag that certificate pinning (a network-security protection) is still inactive because it can only be validated in a full build that was intentionally skipped, and their standing condition is that no real patient data be used until that verification happens — a deployment gate rather than unfinished work inside this commit. That part looks like a reasonable, self-contained fix and is consistent with the idea of fixing a sync problem. However, the commit message says "all edge cases handled now," and the actual change only covers one specific case: a single retry after a dropped connection. The diff doesn't show handling for other failure modes (for example, the retry attempt itself throwing an error is not caught, and a server response that is not OK still just fails), so the "all edge cases" claim overstates what the code actually does. I'm only comparing the message to the diff here, not running the code. There is also no mention or evidence of any testing, and the message refers only to "the sync bug" without naming a specific defect. No story or issue was attributed to this commit; given that the message is vague about which bug it addresses, it would help to have the developer confirm the intended scope and link the relevant story or ticket. Because of the gap between the sweeping "all edge cases" wording and the narrower fix in the diff, this is flagged for a developer's review rather than treated as complete.
